item.title: In-company training: new federal priority until 2028
item.description: SERI is allocating CHF 3 million to strengthen the quality of dual vocational education and training in the period 2026-2028.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New SERI priority area for dual education and training from 2026 to 2028 - Federal budget of CHF 3 million to strengthen the quality of education - Three objectives: awareness-raising, knowledge exchange, project support
## Key Facts - **What**: Priority area In-company training of the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI) - When: 1 September 2026 – end of 2028 - Where: Switzerland, cantonal and national - Who: SERI, cantons, professional organisations - Amount: CHF 3 million - Background: Part of the roadmap Attractiveness of vocational and professional education and training (decided November 2025)
Bern, 1 September 2026 — The State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI) has officially announced the launch of a new priority area for in-company training. The initiative will start on 1 September 2026 and will run until the end of 2028, with a budget of CHF 3 million.
The decision to launch this programme dates back to November 2025, when the partners agreed to include the initiative in the Attractiveness of Vocational and Professional Education and Training roadmap at the national meeting on vocational and professional education and training. SERI is now taking action to consolidate and improve two decisive factors: the willingness of companies to train apprentices and the quality of the training provided.
### In-company training: the focus of dual training
In-company training is at the heart of the Swiss dual vocational education and training system. It enables apprentices to acquire essential practical skills and helps to reduce the need for qualified personnel on the labour market. Quality training encourages young people to choose apprenticeship paths and strengthens the role of companies as excellent training providers.
The priority area is divided into three fundamental objectives. Firstly, to raise awareness among vocational training actors (companies, schools, sector bodies) of the strategic importance of in-company training. Secondly, to promote contacts and the exchange of knowledge between the various parties involved. Finally, to concretely support projects aimed at optimising the quality of training in apprenticeship companies.
Priority topics include strengthening the supervision of apprenticeships, continuing education of in-company trainers, support for young people in difficulty and optimising the framework conditions for apprenticeship companies. Rémy Hübschi, Deputy Director of SERI, comments: With the priority area, the Confederation is making a concrete contribution to ensuring the quality of dual vocational education and training in the long term and making it more attractive for apprentices and apprenticeship companies. I invite the partners to submit their ideas and submit suitable projects. ### How federal funds will be distributed
SERI intends to implement the priority area through close cooperation with the cantons and professional organisations. The federal approach includes four complementary lines of action.
Firstly, SERI will share knowledge and examples of good practice collected at national level, facilitating the exchange of experience between VET actors. Secondly, it will make specific financial resources available to support concrete projects aimed at modernising and improving in-company training.
Federal contributions will be able to finance four types of projects:
- **Preliminary projects**: feasibility studies and needs analysis - Innovative projects: experimentation of new training models - Multiplication projects: dissemination of already established quality practices - Networking projects: initiatives aimed at strengthening connections between actors
The funds will primarily be allocated to the cantons and professional organisations (employers' associations, trade unions, industry bodies), which are SERI's preferred operating partners.
### The impact on Swiss dual education
Strengthening in-company training responds to a growing challenge: to ensure that companies maintain and amplify their willingness to invest in training, despite economic pressures and administrative costs. The quality of practical training is closely related to the completion rate of apprenticeships and the transformation of apprentices into stable employees in the labour market.
In Switzerland, the dual system is an internationally recognised model of excellence. To keep it competitive and attractive, especially for young people, there must be continuous investment in the qualification of in-company trainers and in the updating of practical curricula. This priority area provides the necessary federal support so that the cantons and employers can implement these strategic improvements and ensure long-term employability.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### How to access federal contributions and submit projects
Cantons and professional organisations interested in receiving federal funding must follow an application process. SERI will accept proposals for preliminary, innovative, multiplication and networking projects by the end of 2028, when the priority area ends.
Step 1: Identify the type of project Each applicant must first define which category of project he or she intends to implement. If it is exploratory research on training gaps, choose preliminary project. If the goal is to test a new practical teaching method, opt for an innovative project. If you want to extend an already established good practice to other cantons, choose multiplication project. If you want to create a stable network of education actors, propose a networking project.
**Step 2: Formulate the proposal** The proposal must clearly describe how the project contributes to the three objectives of the priority area: awareness-raising, knowledge exchange and quality optimisation. The budget required, the expected duration and the partners involved in implementation must also be specified.
Step 3: Apply to SERI Proposals must be submitted directly to the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation. Although the source does not specify an intermediate application deadline, projects must be completed by the end of 2028.
### Prospects for companies and trainers
In-company training remains the driving force behind the competitiveness of the Swiss labour market. Investing in the quality of practical preparation means investing in the employability of young people and in solving the need for qualified personnel. In-company trainers will be able to take advantage of federal subsidies to access methodological refresher courses. Companies will have incentives to implement stricter quality controls and to improve their training facilities.
If you would like to learn more about vocational training opportunities in Switzerland, please consult the [opportunità di lavoro](nav:jobs) and [aziende che assumono](nav:companies) apprentices in your sector. For information on salaries and tax benefits linked to apprentice salaries, use the [calcolatore stipendi](nav:calculator) for a personalised estimate.

item.title: The reference mortgage rate remains stable
item.description: The reference mortgage rate in Switzerland remains at 1.25%. The Federal Office for Housing (FOH) confirms the unchanged value from 2 September 2025.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The reference mortgage rate in Switzerland remains at 1.25%. - The value is unchanged as of September 2, 2025. - The Federal Office for Housing (FOH) confirms the rate. - Most tenants have not yet obtained a rent reduction.
## Key Facts - **What**: Reference mortgage rate - When: From September 2, 2025 - Where: Switzerland - Who: Federal Office for Housing (FOH) - Amount: 1.25%
The reference mortgage rate in Switzerland remains at 1.25%. This was announced on Tuesday by the Federal Office for Housing (FOH), pointing out that the value on which rents are based in Switzerland has remained unchanged since 2 September 2025, i.e. for one year. As in the previous quarter, the rate stands at 1.31%. However, since it is published in quarter percentages, the mortgage rate continues to be 1.25% and will remain at this level until the average rate falls below 1.13% or exceeds 1.37%. If the rent is still based on a rate of 1.5% or higher, the FOAB note reads, the right to a rent reduction remains in principle.
### Implications for tenants Despite the fact that the reference mortgage rate fell twice in 2025, the majority of tenants have not yet received a rent reduction. This is according to the Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI), which provides an online calculator to assert their rights. Today, the rate used to calculate rents has remained stable at 1.25%, the ASI recalls in a statement. Good news for tenants? Only partially, because the adjustment mechanism often works one-way: landlords increase their rent when the rate rises, but hardly anyone reduces it when it falls. ## Practical analysis The invariability of the reference mortgage rate has significant implications for the rental market in Switzerland. The FOAB has pointed out that the rate will continue to be 1.25% until the average rate falls below 1.13% or exceeds 1.37%. This means that, for the time being, there will be no significant changes in rents based on this rate.
### Right to rent reduction If the rent is still based on a rate of 1.5% or higher, tenants have the right to demand a rent reduction. However, the ASI has highlighted that most tenants have not yet obtained a rent reduction, despite the fact that the reference mortgage rate fell twice in 2025. This underlines the importance for tenants to be informed about their rights and to use tools such as the ASI's online calculator to assert their claims.
### One-way adjustment mechanism The rent adjustment mechanism often works one-way: landlords increase their rent when the rate rises, but hardly anyone reduces it when it falls. This means that, despite the fact that the reference mortgage rate has remained stable at 1.25%, tenants may not see a reduction in their rents. The ASI pointed out that, in principle, the right to a rent reduction remains if the rent is based on a rate higher than 1.5%.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ## Concrete action For tenants who are in a situation where rent is based on a rate of more than 1.5%, it is important to take steps to enforce their rights. The ASI provides an online calculator that can help tenants determine if they are eligible for a rent reduction. It is crucial for tenants to be informed about their rights and use tools like this to obtain a rent reduction if they are eligible.
### Step-by-step procedure 1. **Check the reference rate**: Check if your rent is based on a rate higher than 1.5%. 2. Using the online calculator: Access the ASI online calculator to determine if you are eligible for a rent reduction. 3. Request the reduction: If the calculator confirms that you are eligible for a reduction, contact your landlord to request a rent reduction. 4. Documentation: Keep all communications and documents related to your request for rent reduction.
### Useful tools ASI offers an online calculator that can help tenants determine if they are eligible for a rent reduction. This tool is available for free and can be used by any tenant who wants to assert their rights.
### Final CTA For more information and to use the ASI's online calculator, visit the website of the Swiss Tenants' Association. This tool can be a valuable ally for tenants who want to obtain a rent reduction and assert their rights.

item.title: Retail trade, sales increase in July
item.description: Swiss retail sales increased by 0.2% in July, an increase of 1.7% in real terms.

## In brief - Sales in the Swiss retail trade increased by 0.2% in July. - In real terms, the increase is 1.7%. - Food products recorded a +0.2%, while the non-food sector fell by 0.1%.
## Key Facts - **What**: Increase in retail sales in Switzerland. - When: July 2025. - Where: Switzerland. - Who: Federal Statistical Office (FSO). - Amount: +0.2% compared to July 2025, +1.7% in real terms.
July proved to be a positive month for Swiss brick-and-mortar and online stores, with sales up 0.2% compared to the same month in 2025, adjusting for different business days and holidays. This figure was released today by the Federal Statistical Office (FSO), which also indicated an increase of 1.7% in real terms, adjusted for inflation.
### Food and beverage products Food, beverages and tobacco increased by 0.2%, which corresponds to +1.2% in real terms. This sector showed significant resilience despite general economic conditions.
### Non-food sector On the other hand, the non-food sector declined by 0.1%, with an increase of 1.0% in real terms. This decline could be attributed to various factors, including consumer preferences and economic conditions.
The monthly statistics provided by the FSO are based on data from a sample of around 3000 companies in the retail sector. Smaller companies are consulted on their monthly turnover at quarterly intervals. ## Practical analysis The increase in retail sales in Switzerland has significant implications for the Swiss economy. An increase of 0.2% compared to July 2025, which corresponds to +1.7% in real terms, indicates a certain stability and resilience of the sector despite general economic conditions.
### Impact on consumers For Swiss consumers, this increase in sales could translate into increased availability of products and services, as well as possible promotions and discounts from stores. However, it is important to note that the non-food sector has experienced a decline of 0.1%, which could affect consumers' purchasing choices.
### Implications for businesses For retail businesses, this increase in sales is a positive sign, but also a challenge. Companies will need to continue to innovate and adapt to consumer preferences in order to maintain their competitiveness. In addition, smaller businesses, which are consulted at quarterly intervals, will need to closely monitor their monthly turnover to adapt to market fluctuations.
### Comparison with the past Compared to previous months, the increase in sales in July 2025 represents a significant improvement. However, it is important to consider that economic conditions can vary greatly from month to month, and businesses must be prepared for any future fluctuations.

item.title: Tenants' association: "it is necessary to ask for a reduction in rent"
item.description: The benchmark mortgage rate fell twice in 2025, but most tenants did not get a rent reduction.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The benchmark mortgage rate fell twice in 2025. - Most tenants did not get a rent reduction. - The Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI) calls for a reduction.
## Key Facts - **What**: Rent reduction due to the drop in mortgage rate. - When: March and September 2025. - Where: Switzerland. - Who: Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI). - Amount: Reduction of about 3% for each variation of a quarter of a percentage point.
The benchmark mortgage rate, which is used to calculate rents, fell twice in 2025, but most tenants have not yet achieved a rent reduction. The Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI) reported that despite the rate remaining stable at 1.25%, landlords increase their rent when the rate rises, but hardly anyone reduces it when it falls.
The ASI has made an online calculator available to assert your rights. The reference rate is recalculated every quarter on the average of the mortgage rates charged by the banks. In 2023, the rate had risen from 1.25% to 1.75%, leading to price increases for many households. Then, in March 2025, it fell to 1.5% and finally to 1.25% last September.
Any change of a quarter of a percentage point in the interest rate generally entitles you to a rent reduction of around 3%. However, only a minority of tenants have been able to benefit from the discount so far. According to data from Zurich Kantonalbank (ZKB), only 12% of tenants had formally requested the second reduction in April this year.
Faced with this inertia, the ASI calls on landlords to proactively pass on rate reductions, without offsetting them with flat-rate increases in ancillary costs. But in practice, the association argues, tenants often have no choice but to take action themselves. For this reason, a rent calculator has been developed, available on the www.asi-infoalloggio.ch website, which allows you to check in a few clicks whether you are entitled to a discount and quantify it.
The ASI has also published a section with questions and answers; it also invites those who have doubts to contact their regional sections. The recommendation is clear: do not wait for the owner to come forward, but check your contract immediately and possibly actively ask for a reduction in the rent. ## Practical implications
The current situation highlights a disparity in the rent adjustment mechanism in Switzerland. While landlords are quick to raise rents when mortgage rates rise, they are less prompt to reduce them when rates fall. This places a greater financial burden on tenants, who see their living costs rise without a corresponding downward adjustment.
The ASI emphasizes the importance of greater transparency and proactivity on the part of landlords. Landlords should be incentivized to pass on mortgage rate reductions to tenants in a timely manner, avoiding offsetting these reductions with flat-rate increases in ancillary costs. This approach would not only help tenants save money but also help maintain a balance in the rental market.
For tenants, it is crucial to know their rights and use the tools available to enforce them. The ASI rent calculator is a valuable tool that allows you to quickly check if you are entitled to a rent reduction and quantify the amount. In addition, the ASI offers a section with questions and answers and invites tenants to contact the regional sections for further clarification.
## Comparison with the previous situation
Before the fall in mortgage rates in 2025, many tenants had seen their rents rise due to the increase in the reference rate. This has led to an increase in the cost of living for many Swiss households. With the fall in interest rates, a reduction in rents was expected, but so far only a minority of tenants have been able to benefit from this reduction.
The current situation underlines the importance of increased vigilance on the part of tenants and greater transparency on the part of landlords. Only through closer cooperation and greater awareness of tenants' rights will it be possible to ensure a fairer and more transparent rental market.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ## Actions to take
If you are a tenant and want to check if you are entitled to a rent reduction, you can use the rent calculator available on the www.asi-infoalloggio.ch website. This tool allows you to quickly check if you are entitled to a discount and quantify the amount.
In addition, the ASI offers a section with questions and answers and invites tenants to contact the regional sections for further clarification. The recommendation is clear: do not wait for the landlord to come forward, but check your contract immediately and possibly actively ask for a rent reduction.
## Step-by-step procedure
1. Check your contract: Check your rental agreement to see if you're eligible for a rent reduction. 2. Use the rent calculator: Go to the www.asi-infoalloggio.ch website and use the calculator to check if you are eligible for a rebate and to quantify the amount. 3. Contact the ASI: If you have any doubts or need further clarification, contact the regional sections of the ASI for assistance. 4. Request the reduction: If you are eligible for a rent reduction, contact your landlord and actively request a rent reduction.

- Rent calculator: [Calcolatore dell'affitto](nav:calculator) - Q&A section: Questions & Answers - Regional contacts: ASI regional sections

item.title: Reference mortgage rate remains at 1.25%: what changes for rents
item.description: FOAB confirms the parameter at 1.25% for the third quarter: historic low, average mortgage rate at 1.31%, SNB stuck at 0.0%. What happens now for tenants and landlords.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Reference mortgage rate confirmed at 1.25% - The indicator is at an all-time low for a year now - SNB maintains key interest rate at 0.0%, inflation at 0.4% - Average mortgage interest rate at 1.31%, unchanged
## Key Facts - **What**: Reference mortgage rate confirmed at 1.25% - When: Quarterly decision of the FOAB, published today - Where: whole Switzerland (single national parameter) - Who: Federal Office for Housing (FOH) - Amount: 1.25% (policy rate), 1.31% (average rate), 0.0% (SNB policy rate), 0.4% (July inflation) - Thresholds: Automatic triggers if average falls below 1.13% or exceeds 1.37%
The reference mortgage rate does not change: the indicator used to determine rents for rental apartments throughout Switzerland remains at 1.25%. This was announced by the Federal Office for Housing (FOH) this morning, confirming the forecasts of all economists interviewed by the AWP agency, who had predicted the status quo.
### A level that has stood for twelve months The parameter has been at this level, which has also been its lowest level for a year now. Today's decision is part of a very firm general interest rate picture, with the Swiss National Bank (SNB) maintaining its key interest rate at 0.0%. However, experts do not rule out a possible rise, in the wake of inflation which, although still under control (inflation in July was at 0.4%), shows signs of progress.
### How to calculate the parameter Published quarterly, the indicator calculated by the FOAB is based on an average interest rate for Swiss mortgage loans, weighted by volume of loans, and is set in quarters of a percentage point. The average interest rate on 30 June remained at 1.31%, as in the previous quarter. With commercial rounding, the reference rate, which is decisive from the point of view of tenancy law, continues to be 1.25%. It will remain at this level until the average interest rate falls below 1.13% or exceeds 1.37%.
[Link contestuale: per chi vuole simulare l'impatto sul proprio budget, è disponibile il calcolatore dello [stipendio netto](nav:calculator)]. ### What changes for tenants If the rent is still based on a rate of 1.5% or higher, the right to a rent reduction remains in principle. To put this in context: if the reference rate rises by 0.25 percentage points, landlords can increase the rent by 3.00%; in the opposite case, tenants have the option of requesting a rent reduction of 2.91%. With the parameter stuck at 1.25%, those who are already aligned with this percentage see no changes, while those who pay a rent calculated on higher previous values retain the option of applying to the conciliation authority for a discount.
### A history of downward movements Since September 2008, the reference mortgage rate has been unified throughout Switzerland and has replaced the previously decisive rate for variable-rate mortgages in the individual cantons. The rate started at a peak of 3.5% and had fallen to a low of 1.25% for the first time in March 2020. In 2023, there were then two hikes, the first ever forward movements of the indicator, which brought the parameter to 1.75%, a level maintained between December 2023 and December 2024, when it had fallen to 1.5%. The last downward jump dates back to twelve months ago.
### Outlook to 2027-2028 According to experts, the current rate of 1.25% could remain relatively long until 2027-2028, provided that major geopolitical or economic events do not give a strong boost to inflation, resulting in an increase in the SNB's key interest rate and, in turn, an increase in mortgage rates. For Swiss landlords and tenants, a phase of prolonged stability is therefore beginning, which allows them to plan family budgets with greater certainty, but which could come to an abrupt end in the event of external shocks.
[Link contestuale: per valutare l'effetto sulle proprie finanze personali, può essere utile consultare il comparatore del [costo della vita in Svizzera](nav:cost-of-living)].
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### How the request for rent reduction works If you wish to assert your right to a rent reduction, the procedure involves sending a formal request to the landlord, indicating the current reference rate (1.25%) and the current rent calculated at a rate of 1.5% or higher. If the landlord refuses or does not reside within the deadline, the tenant can contact the cantonal conciliation authority within 30 days of the dispute. It is advisable to keep all documentation: lease agreement, previous notices and references to federal tenancy law.
### When to expect the next update The indicator is published quarterly by the FOAB. The next revision is expected in the months following 30 September, the reference date for calculating the next average rate. If the average interest rate were to fall below 1.13%, the parameter would rise to 1.00%; if it were to exceed 1.37%, it would rise to 1.50%.
### Useful tools for tenants and landlords If you want to simulate the impact of a possible rent increase of 3.00% or a reduction of 2.91% on your monthly budget, you can use the tools available on the website. For those who are considering buying a property, it is useful to consult the [stipendio netto](nav:calculator) calculator to check the affordability of the mortgage payments compared to disposable income.
[CTA finale: per pianificare il budget familiare e capire quanto incide il canone sullo stipendio, usa il [calcolatore dello stipendio](nav:calculator).]

item.title: Customs, new digital tools for goods and purchases
item.description: DaziT concludes at the end of 2026 with Passar and QuickZoll. Simplification of cross-border traffic, modernized border controls.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - DaziT concludes at the end of 2026 with over 40 apps and 250 microservices - Passar simplifies cross-border trade freight traffic - QuickZoll speeds up customs clearance for private purchases - HTSV modernization and border control systems
## Key Facts - **What**: FOCBS Digital Transformation Programme for Customs (DaziT) - When: End of the year 2026 - Where: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) - Who: Karin Keller-Sutter (Federal Councillor), Christoph Mäder (President economiesuisse) - Reach: Over 40 applications, approximately 250 microservices
The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security's (FOCBS) IT transformation programme DaziT will be completed at the end of the year. The announcement was made in Basel on Tuesday by Federal Councillor Karin Keller-Sutter and economiesuisse President Christoph Mäder. This programme enables the Confederation to collect revenue more effectively by strengthening border security and improving the framework conditions for the Swiss economy.
The FOCBS's IT environment has been completely modernised. The programme has introduced more than 40 specialised applications, consisting of around 250 microservices. This is a structural intervention that transforms the way Switzerland manages cross-border freight traffic and customs control.
### New platforms for businesses and individuals
Companies and private individuals now have two new digital services at their disposal. The "Passar" platform simplifies the cross-border traffic of commercial goods. The "QuickZoll" app speeds up customs clearance for private purchases and enables electronic tagging. Both services significantly reduce time and administrative complexity for those who trade or buy across borders.
In addition to the two main platforms, DaziT has modernized the performance-related heavy vehicle charge system and border control systems. This reform of the Federal Customs represents a radical change in Swiss border management, based on automation, digital traceability and more efficient controls.
[Approfondisci il costo della vita transfrontaliera](nav:cost-of-living) to understand how customs simplification impacts your international purchases. ## Practical implications: what really changes
The modernisation of the DaziT programme is not just an administrative matter: it has concrete implications for companies and private individuals operating across borders. The digital transformation of the Federal Customs translates into measurable benefits in daily work.
### Operational simplification for companies
Swiss companies that trade cross-border goods benefit from the Passar platform in a tangible way. Processes that used to require manual intervention and paper checks are now automated. Digital traceability makes it possible to identify packages, quantities and recipients in real time. For regular exporters or importers, this means reduced customs times, lower downtime costs and predictable transits. Customs agents and freight forwarders gain operational speed and reduce the risk of administrative errors. A company transporting components from Zurich to Italy benefits from smoother controls at the Ticino border.
### Expedited Private Customs Clearance
Private individuals who buy online abroad or receive international parcels implicitly use QuickZoll. The electronic marking allows for a more streamlined process: the package is digitally identified, customs processes it automatically when possible, and collection is accelerated. Those who buy from European sites and have to pay VAT on collection benefit from a unique and digitally tracked process, without duplication of documentation or bureaucratic delays.
### Modernisation of the heavy vehicle charge
The performance-related heavy vehicle charge (HTSV) has been modernised in the DaziT programme. Heavy-duty vehicles are tracked and taxed on the basis of actual performance, not on rough estimates. This means more precision in tax calculations and better transparency for Swiss transport operators. Digitalisation reduces calculation errors and simplifies reporting.
### Smart and targeted border controls
Swiss border control systems have been updated with intelligent risk criteria. Checks are no longer random, but geared towards high-risk situations: customs fraud, irregular imports, violations of security regulations. Legitimate flows are disposed of quickly, security controls are targeted where they are really needed. This allows operational speed without compromising on protection.
### Comparison: before and after DaziT
Before transformation: Outdated IT systems, widespread manual procedures, unpredictable clearance times, high risk of errors. After DaziT: Automated processes, real-time data, intelligent controls, smooth operations. It doesn't eliminate security controls, but makes them more effective.

## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## How to use Passar and QuickZoll: operating guide
Now that the DaziT programme is in operation, businesses and individuals need to know how to take advantage of the new tools. The procedures are simple, but it is useful to know the main steps to get the most out of it.
Companies wishing to use the Passar platform must register with the FOCBS via official channels. The platform is dedicated to cross-border trade traffic: suppliers, exporters, importers and customs brokers log in with federated credentials. Once registered, companies upload shipment data (consignees, quantity, goods description, declared value), and the system automatically processes most of the checks. Manual testing is carried out according to risk criteria, not in random bulk. For shippers and customs brokers, this simplification represents a significant gain in clearance speed and reduction in administrative and downtime costs.
### QuickZoll for private individuals and electronic cash on delivery
Private individuals who receive parcels from abroad already implicitly use QuickZoll. When a parcel enters Switzerland, the courier or customs automatically generates an electronic sticker via the app. For the private individual, the process is invisible in most cases: the parcel is processed automatically by the system, and if there are no security problems, it arrives at its destination without any further formalities. If there is VAT to be paid on a purchase (e.g. clothing or electronics from an EU website), the system calculates the tax and communicates it to the recipient, with simplified payment at the courier collection.
### Official information and technical support
The FOCBS provides official support via the Federal Customs website. Detailed instructions on Passar, QuickZoll and the HTSV tax are published in the FOCBS's information portals. Customs brokers, freight forwarders and registered companies can find technical documentation, webinars, and dedicated support forums. For private individuals, FAQs and practical guides are also available from carriers (Swiss Post, DHL, UPS, etc.) that use QuickZoll as an operating standard.
### Completion history
The DaziT program ends at the end of 2026. This means that the complete rollout of the 40+ applications will be completed by the end of the year. In the meantime, Passar and QuickZoll are already up and running. There are no mandatory deadlines to migrate legacy systems, but early access offers competitive advantages: those who adopt Passar immediately gain speed compared to waiting competitors.
### Integration with federal tax management
The modernisation of the FOCBS also improves communication between customs and other federal bodies (FTA/ESTV for direct federal taxes and VAT). item.title: Rents: rate down but the reduction is not automatic
item.description: In 2025, the reference mortgage interest rate fell twice. Only 12% of tenants requested the reduction. The ASI reminds that it pays to actively request the reduction.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In 2025, the key interest rate fell twice: to 1.5% (March) and 1.25% (September) - Every drop of 0.25% results in about a 3% reduction on the rent - Only 12% of tenants requested the second lowering (April 2026) - Automatic adjustment works one-way: owners raise, rarely lower
## Key Facts - **What**: Rent reduction due to the fall in the reference mortgage rate - When: March and September 2025 - Where: Throughout Switzerland (all regions) - Who: Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI); data from Zürcher Kantonalbank (ZKB) - Amount: Approx. 3% rent reduction for every 0.25% interest rate drop
In 2025, the reference mortgage rate fell twice, creating the conditions for rent reductions. However, the reality of Swiss tenants tells a different story: the majority have not yet submitted a formal request to the landlord. According to the Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI), it is time to remember a fundamental principle: the rent adjustment does not automatically take place downwards.
The rate used to calculate rents has remained stable at 1.25%, according to a statement from ASI today. But the road traveled so far has been anything but linear. In 2023, the rate had risen from 1.25% to 1.75%, generating price increases for millions of Swiss tenants. Then, in March 2025, the rate fell to 1.5%. Finally, last September it reached 1.25%, the pre-crisis level. Two cuts in one year: a real opportunity to obtain rent reductions.
### The calculation mechanism
Any change of a quarter of a percentage point (0.25%) in the rate generally entitles you to a rent reduction of around 3%. This means that tenants should have benefited from two successive reductions: one at the time of the drop from 1.75% to 1.5%, another when the rate fell from 1.5% to 1.25%. In total, the overall drop of half a point (0.5%) is expected to correspond to a reduction of around 6% on the monthly rent.
But there is a problem. According to data from Zurich Kantonalbank, in April of this year, only 12% of tenants had formally requested the second reduction. This figure illustrates a huge gap between the reductions that should occur and those that are actually achieved. The ASI is clear: "The automatic adjustment works one-way." Landlords increase their rent when the rate rises, accelerating price increases. They rarely reduce it when the rate falls.
The reason for this is simple: there is no automatic mechanism that obliges landlords to pass on reductions to tenants. The Tenancy Act (Code of Obligations, Art. 253 et seq.) allows adjustments based on changes in the interest rate, but the procedure remains manual. The landlord must consciously decide to notify a reduction; the tenant, in the meantime, must be vigilant and actively request. ### Why the system favors owners
The asymmetry between price increases and reductions is not accidental. When the rate rises, the owner has an immediate economic incentive: passing on the increase to the tenant protects his margins. The owner's statement arrives on time. When the rate falls, the incentive disappears: reducing the rent means lower income, and the owner without regulatory constraints can simply ignore the situation.
The ASI notes that landlords, while not applying the rent reduction, often compensate with flat-rate increases on ancillary costs (heating, maintenance, insurance). The net result for the tenant is a minimal or non-existent reduction, despite the fact that the interest rate has fallen. In other cases, the landlord is simply late, waiting for the right time to negotiate other contractual conditions.
For this reason, the ASI reminds tenants that it is not enough to wait: they must act. The same association calls on landlords to proactively pass on the reductions without compensating them with flat-rate increases on ancillary costs. But, in practice, the association argues, tenants have no choice but to take action themselves.
### The calculator as a tool for awareness
Recognizing this reality, the ASI has made available a free [calcolatore online](nav:calculator), available on the www.asi-infoalloggio.ch website, which allows you to check in a few clicks if you are entitled to a discount and to quantify it. The tool asks for a few data: the current rent, the rate at the time of signing the contract, the current rate, and the date of the last adjustment. In seconds, the calculator provides the exact amount of the reduction due.
ASI has also published a section with questions and answers, designed to guide those who face the problem for the first time. The regional sections of the association remain available for more in-depth advice. The invitation is clear and direct: do not wait for the owner to come forward, but check your contract immediately and possibly actively ask for a rent reduction.
This approach transforms the tenant from a taxable person into a conscious actor. Knowing the right and the exact number is not a luxury, but a necessity in a system where regulatory asymmetry in fact favors the inertia of the owners. The reference rate is recalculated every quarter on the average of the mortgage rates charged by the banks, which means that updates can occur at regular intervals and tenants should monitor their right periodically.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### How to request and obtain the reduction
The first step is always the contract. Check to see if it contains an adjustment clause based on the reference mortgage rate. Not all contracts include it; if there is not, a reduction becomes more difficult (but not impossible) to enforce. With the contract at hand, access the ASI calculator and collect the necessary data: the original monthly fee, the rate at the time of subscription, the current rate. The calculator will do the rest.
Once the amount due has been calculated, document the result. Screenshots, printouts, notes: everything that proves the right to the reduction. Then, contact the owner. The ASI recommends sending a written request — by registered email or simple letter — that clearly mentions the change in the reference rate (from 1.75% to 1.25%, passing through 1.5%), the amount of the calculated reduction (about 3% for every 0.25% decrease), the date from which the reduction must take effect, and the date by which the owner should respond.
If the landlord does not respond, or refuses, contact the regional branch of the ASI in your canton. The association offers free advice and, if necessary, support in conciliation procedures. Many cantons have a conciliation authority — a public office that attempts to resolve disputes between tenant and landlord before the case reaches the court. It is a quick procedure, often free of charge for the tenant, and resolves most cases.
### Don't put it off: your rights
Remember that the right to a reduction is retroactive. If the rate fell as early as March 2025, and we are now in September 2026, you may be entitled to an 18-month reduction in arrears. It is an additional incentive not to postpone: each month of inaction corresponds to months of full rent that you should have paid less.
There is no legal deadline for requesting the reduction, but the principle is simple: the sooner you ask, the sooner you get. The landlord has no obligation to voluntarily inform the tenant of a reduction that is due. The Tenancy Act (Code of Obligations, Art. 253 et seq.) lays down the rules for adjustment, but does not oblige the landlord to take the initiative. It is the tenant who must supervise and request.
The ASI estimates that millions of francs remain in the pockets of landlords every year, while they should return to tenants in the form of reduced rents. This is not a matter of courtesy: it is a matter of rights enshrined in federal tenancy law. Using the ASI's [calcolatore online](nav:calculator) is free, fast and anonymous. Asking the landlord only costs an email or a letter. Don't put it off any longer.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/attualita/1947247/inquilini-riduzione-affitto-associazione-asi)*

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 73% of Swiss people call for measures against global warming - 80% in favor of energy renovation of buildings - 62% support more financial support for agriculture
## Key Facts - **What**: Survey on measures against global warming - When: August 19-20, 2024 - Where: Switzerland - Who: 20 Minuten and Tamedia - Amount: 73% of respondents
After the summer heatwave, the Swiss are calling for concrete measures, such as the renovation of buildings or the installation of solar panels. This is what emerges from a survey by the online newspaper 20 Minuten and the publisher Tamedia published today. For almost three-quarters of respondents, it is urgent to take measures against global warming. A quarter, on the other hand, do not see the need to do more. Support for strengthening environmental policy is significantly higher among women (60%) than among men (43%).
### Energy renovation of buildings The energy renovation of buildings and the improvement of their insulation are the most widely supported. Four out of five respondents are in favour. The measure even meets with unanimous support across political divisions: it is supported by 89% of Green supporters and 72% of SVP supporters.
### Financial support for agriculture Increased financial support from the federal government for agriculture to compensate for losses caused by heat and drought is also convincing for 62% of respondents. In addition, 58% would like the federal government to promote night trains more.
### Popular initiatives A number of popular initiatives are also well received. The Greens' "For a secure supply of renewable energies (Solar Initiative)", which aims to make solar systems compulsory on new buildings and when renovating roofs, received 71% of "yes" or "rather yes" votes. The Federal Council recommends rejecting it.
The popular initiative "For a sustainable and future-oriented Swiss financial centre (Financial Centre Initiative)", on the other hand, received 58% support: a third of respondents were clearly in favour and a quarter were in favour. The text calls on the Confederation to ensure that the Swiss financial centre is geared towards ecological objectives in line with international standards. The Federal Council recently voted against it.
Finally, 61% of respondents are in favour or rather in favour of the initiative of the environmental organisation Traffic "For strong public transport and fair air fares (Mobility Voucher Initiative)", which provides in particular for a tax on airline tickets. The collection of signatures is still ongoing. ## Practical analysis The survey reveals a significant gender split in support for environmental measures. Women are more likely to support a strengthening of environmental policy than men. This could influence future policy decisions and priorities of the federal government.
### Implications for the energy renovation of buildings Strong support for the energy renovation of buildings could lead to new policies and incentives for the renovation and installation of solar panels. This could have a significant impact on the construction sector and employment in this sector.
### Support for agriculture Financial support for agriculture could help farmers recoup losses caused by heat and drought. This could also lead to greater sustainability in the agricultural sector, with the adoption of practices that are more resilient to climate change.

item.title: Swiss Life cuts 600 posts by 2028
item.description: Swiss insurance company reduces headcount through natural replacement. 200 reductions already started, another 100 by the end of 2026. Impact on the labor market.

## In brief - Swiss Life plans to cut around 600 jobs by 2028 - Swiss Life Switzerland and Asset Managers, mainly foreign - 200 reductions already started: 100 completed, another 100 by the end of 2026 - Digitalization and natural turnover as the main tools
## Key Facts - **What**: Organisational downsizing of Swiss Life - When: 2028 (final goal); 200 already reduced/scheduled by the end of 2026 - Where: Swiss Life Switzerland and Asset Managers, with a focus on foreign countries - Who: Swiss Life Insurance Company - Current headcount: Approximately 11,000 employees - Method: Natural turnover and targeted selection in recruitment - Support: Career reorientation for affected employees
The Swiss Life insurance company has announced its intention to reduce the number of its employees by around 600 by 2028. The downsizing will affect both Swiss Life Switzerland and Swiss Life Asset Managers, with a major impact on foreign activities. The company, which currently has around 11,000 employees, has already started the reduction process.
### The reduction process has already started
Thanks to targeted recruitment for vacant positions, around 100 jobs have already been reduced. A further 100 posts are expected to follow by the end of 2026, according to the timetable communicated by the company. The overall reduction of 600 posts is therefore a multi-year process, not an immediate cut.
A large part of the cuts will be made through "natural staff turnover", the main mechanism identified by Swiss Life. This approach makes it possible to reduce the workforce progressively, without resorting to mass collective redundancies.
### Motivations and digitalization
Swiss Life justifies this decision with the need to ensure the "profitable expansion of the business beyond 2027 and the necessary increase in efficiency, also thanks to the opportunities offered by progressive digitization". Digital transformation is the strategic driver behind the downsizing plan.
Employees affected by the restructuring will be supported in their professional reorientation. The company has emphasized this aspect in official communications, implying that support for the employment transition will be a central element of the process. ### Why the Swiss insurance industry is changing
Swiss Life's decision reflects a broader transformation underway in the Swiss financial and insurance sector. Automation and digitalisation are transforming the way companies manage operations, reducing the demand for staff dedicated to back-office activities and administrative processes. Swiss Life, like other large insurance companies, is having to adapt its organisational structure to remain competitive.
The "progressive digitalisation" mentioned by Swiss Life includes: - Automation of data processing and document management - Implementation of artificial intelligence systems for risk assessment and pricing - Shift of services to self-service digital platforms for customers - Consolidation of service centers towards more efficient economies of scale
These transformations make it possible to maintain or increase the volumes of work managed with a smaller number of employees, hence the need to downsize the workforce.
### How natural turnover works
Natural turnover is a strategy to contain the employment impact that differs from traditional collective redundancies. When an employee retires, spontaneously leaves the company for other opportunities, or ends a temporary contract, the role is not automatically recreated. Instead, responsibilities are redistributed, merged, or automated.
This method enables Swiss Life to: - Achieve the numerical reduction targets gradually (in the case of Swiss Life, distributed until 2028) - Avoid individual dismissal procedures for economic reasons - Maintain a more stable organizational climate - Give departments time to reorganize and train the remaining staff
"Targeted recruitment for vacant positions" is the complementary lever: not all vacant positions are recreated, but only those that are strategic for the company's future plan.
### Implications for the national labour market
For the Swiss labour market, Swiss Life's plan represents a reduction in the demand for employment in the insurance sector. However, the impact is mitigated by the fact that the process is spread over time until 2028, not concentrated, and will take place "mainly abroad", limiting the impact on jobs in Switzerland. Affected employees will be able to access public employment services at [aziende che assumono nel settore assicurativo](nav:companies) and receive support in finding new jobs, both by the company and by public institutions.

If you are a Swiss Life employee and believe that your position could be affected by the downsizing plan, there are concrete steps you can take to protect your interests and prepare for possible scenarios.
First, consider how your position fits into the context of the communicated plan. The natural turnover will mainly concern retirements and spontaneous exits. If you are close to retirement age according to the AHV criteria (currently 65 for men, 64 for women in transition), you could be a natural candidate for incentivized retirement offers.
### Check your contractual rights
Immediately consult your collective employment agreement (CEA) with Swiss Life, which must contain specific clauses on: - Minimum notice and deadlines for dismissals for economic reasons - Entitlement to severance pay (minimum guaranteed amount) - Support in finding new employment provided by the company - Employment protection period after official notification of downsizing
Most CEAs in the Swiss insurance industry include protections that require the company to communicate in advance and offer support to affected employees. These guarantees are negotiated by trade unions and vary in detail depending on the specific contract.

The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) manages the regional employment offices (URE) in each canton. If you lose your job, registration with the URE is essential:

### Developing digital skills
Digitalisation is the driver of Swiss Life's decline. Digital skills (data analysis, CRM software management, process automation, basic cybersecurity) will be increasingly valuable in the Swiss insurance market.

item.title: L Fribourg permit: validity, extension and requirements
item.description: The short-term L permit in the Canton of Fribourg is valid for a maximum of one year and can be renewed under specific conditions. Find out about duration, extension and constraints.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - L permit: maximum validity 1 year, renewable - Application at the Cantonal Office of Fribourg - Constraints related to the specific employer - Extension: conditions verified by the authorities
## Key Facts - **Type**: Short-term permit for foreigners - Validity: Maximum 1 year for a single issue - Canton: Fribourg (local management and renewal) - Who: Foreign workers on temporary contracts - Action: Request before the start of work - Extension: Renewable if conditions persist - Limit: Cannot be extended indefinitely
The short-term L permit is an authorization document for foreigners who intend to stay and work in Switzerland for limited periods. In the Canton of Fribourg, as in the other Swiss cantons, this permit is regulated by the Federal Act on Foreigners and managed locally by the competent cantonal office.
The maximum duration of the L permit is one year. This period is set at federal level by the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) and applies uniformly in all cantons, including Fribourg. In contrast to the B permit, which can be renewed under general conditions, the L permit is specifically designed for temporary stays and involves stricter constraints: in particular, the close link with the employer who initiated the application.
### When L permission is needed
The L permit becomes mandatory if a foreigner wants to work in Switzerland on a fixed-term contract or for a temporary assignment. In the canton of Fribourg, the application must be submitted before the start of work. The cantonal authorities check whether the conditions laid down by federal law are met: availability of a job, adequacy of the salary to local standards, and the employer's ability to guarantee the expected employment conditions.
### Difference with other permissions
At the Swiss national level, there are four main categories of foreign permits. The L permit is the most restrictive in terms of duration and constraints on the employer. The B (residence) permit is renewable and is usually granted to foreigners with permanent contracts or situations of more stable roots, with different implications on the [costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living) and the economic stability of the household. The C (settlement) permit is reserved for those who have accumulated at least 10 years of legal residence in Switzerland (5 years if an EU/EFTA citizen) and represents the maximum stability status before ordinary naturalization, which requires an additional 10 years of residence plus cantonal and municipal requirements. ### Extension conditions in the canton of Fribourg
An extension of the L permit in the canton of Fribourg is possible, but it is not automatic. The cantonal authorities assess whether the original reasons for the application persist. If the foreign national continues to work for the same employer and the contract has been renewed, the extension may be granted for a further annual period.
However, the L permit cannot be extended indefinitely. After a few years of continuous residence (the precise limit varies according to cantonal and federal legislation), the permit must be converted into a B permit or the foreigner must return to the country of origin. This mechanism ensures that the L permit effectively remains an instrument for temporary stays, and does not become a hidden form of permanent residence.
### Employer constraints
A key aspect of the L permit is the mandatory connection with the employer who initiated the application. The foreigner cannot freely change employment during the period of validity of the permit. If the employment relationship is terminated, the L permit holder loses the legal basis for residence and must leave Switzerland.
This constraint reflects the temporary and instrumental nature of the permit: it is not an independent residence, but an authorization conditional on the continuation of a specific employment relationship. In the Canton of Fribourg, as in all cantons, the authorities may order the revocation of the permit if a violation of this fundamental condition is found. During the stay with an L permit, the worker remains subject to the [AVS/LPP](nav:pension) contributions like any Swiss worker, guaranteeing social security coverage.
### Upgrade to B or C permit
A foreigner holding an L permit in the canton of Fribourg can apply for a change to a B permit if his employment situation stabilizes (e.g. he changes to an open-ended contract) and if the cantonal authorities consider that the legal prerequisites are met. The transition from L to B is not automatic, but requires a new assessment.
To switch to a C permit, it is necessary to accumulate at least 10 years of continuous legal residence in Switzerland (term reduced to 5 years for EU/EFTA citizens). Throughout this period, the person must maintain the legality of the residence, a stable source of income and compliance with Swiss laws. The C permit represents the first step towards full integration and opens up the possibility of subsequent access to ordinary naturalization.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to apply for an L permit in the Canton of Fribourg
The procedure for obtaining an L permit in the Canton of Fribourg follows a standardized federal process, with local management by the Cantonal Immigration Office. The main steps are:
**1. Submission of the application**: The employer or his/her advisor submits the application to the Cantonal Office of Fribourg before the foreigner enters Switzerland. The application must include a preliminary employment contract, the applicant's identity documents and educational qualifications, and an application form completed according to the instructions provided by the office.
2. Administrative verification: The cantonal authorities check that the employer is in good standing, that the workplace has not been published on the Swiss market on time, and that the proposed salary complies with local standards.
3. Decision: If the application is complete and compliant, the cantonal office issues an entry and residence permit for the specified duration (up to a maximum of one year).
4. Issuance of the permit: The foreigner receives the L permit at the federal level (managed by the SEM) and can start work.
### Documents Required
Check with the Cantonal Office of Fribourg for the complete and up-to-date list. Generally, the following are required: signed employment contract, valid passport or identity document, certificates of competence and diplomas (if required by the employer), any criminal records from the country of origin, declaration from the employer on economic capacity.
### Extension and renewal
To renew the L permit, the application must be submitted to the same cantonal office at least 30 days before the expiry date (the precise deadline must be checked locally). The renewal application must prove that the employment relationship continues and that the initial conditions are still met.
Contact the Cantonal Immigration Office Fribourg to receive updated forms and to check the exact deadlines for submission. Use our [calcolatore stipendi](nav:calculator) to check if the proposed amount is within Swiss regional standards and to plan your budget during your temporary stay.

item.title: Hospital bills: why they don't explain everything
item.description: Since 2012, DRG has been hiding diagnoses in the invoice received. How to ask the hospital for clarification and dispute with the health insurer.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Hospital bills don't show diagnoses and walkthroughs - DRG financing system since 2012: hospital does not bill individual services - Diagnoses transformed into classification codes in the SwissDRG catalogue - Patient should ask for coding report to understand clinical details
## Key Facts - **What**: Hospital bills that omit clinical details about diagnoses and procedures - When: Starting from 2012 (introduction of the financing system) - Where: Swiss hospitals (all acute admissions) - Who: Hospitals, hospitals, SwissDRG, Swiss Patient Organisation - Tool: DRG (Diagnosis-Related Groups) catalog; classification into predefined categories
How much can you really understand from a hospital bill received in Switzerland? In theory, the principle is simple: after a hospitalization, the patient receives a copy of the document and can check how much he has been charged, check for any errors and understand the composition of the expense. A mechanism designed to ensure transparency.
In practice, however, the situation is much more complex. For those who are unfamiliar with how the Swiss healthcare system works, it can be almost impossible to reconstruct where the figures on the bill come from. The main reason: the financing system introduced in 2012.
For acute hospitalizations, hospitals do not simply bill for every single service performed. Instead, the patient is placed in a category based on the diagnosis and procedures performed. That category corresponds to a predetermined amount.
### How the DRG system works
After discharge, the clinical information is converted into codes. These allow hospitalization to be classified together with other cases that are considered medically similar. Each group corresponds to a certain cost, which is then related to the basic rate of the hospital.
This is where another important variable comes into play: the basic tariff is not necessarily the same in all Swiss hospitals. It is renegotiated every year and can differ from one facility to another. The final bill amount thus represents a significant element of the healthcare costs for the patient. According to Simon Hölzer, CEO of SwissDRG, "different costs can arise for the same clinical case depending on the facility."
### The information gap on the invoice
The invoice that the patient receives can be formally corrected and verifiable through the SwissDRG catalog. But it does not tell the entire path that led to that figure. In fact, the document does not report the diagnoses and detailed procedures used to determine the code assigned to hospitalization.
To better understand the process, it is therefore necessary to request additional documentation from the hospital, such as the coding report or the discharge report. The decision not to include all the details in the invoice is also partly related to data protection. As Hölzer points out, "an invoice is an administrative document that is often processed by non-medical personnel." Including sensitive diagnoses in a document managed by several people would entail risks of privacy violations.
It is not surprising that hospital bills are a frequent source of questions for the Swiss Patients' Organisation. In case of doubt, the first point of contact is the hospital's billing department. ### The role of the health insurer
If you are unable to clarify directly with the hospital, you can also contact your insurer [malattia](nav:health). According to the health insurance association Prio Swiss, insured persons have the right to request a review of the invoice. Any corrections are made, but "often discreetly and not always visible to the insured person".
This aspect reveals a structural limitation of the system: the control of hospital bills does not necessarily take place in a transparent way towards the patient. The insurer's review takes place behind the scenes, without the patient always being informed of the outcome or the changes made. It is a situation that does not help the patient's understanding, even if formally the right to dispute is guaranteed.
### Transparency vs. data protection
There is an unresolved conflict between two fundamental needs: transparency towards the patient and the protection of personal data. If the invoice included detailed diagnoses and specific procedures, the document would become more understandable but would circulate among more people (administrative staff, back-office staff, possible intermediaries), increasing the risk of leakage of sensitive information.
Hospitals and healthcare providers have opted for a trade-off: keeping clinical details out of the printed bill, forcing the patient to actively request additional documentation if they want to understand the classification. It's a trade-off that prioritizes the security of personal data over the immediate convenience of understanding.
### Trust as the basis of the system
This operational choice means that the Swiss hospital billing system is fundamentally based on trust. The patient receives a document that says "you have received services, here is the amount", but does not have the immediate means to independently verify the correctness of the categorization and the tariff applied.
The Swiss Patients' Organization has clearly pointed out the problem: the system is not transparent. A law professor quoted in the source also admits the same thing. The official recognition that the mechanism does not work perfectly in terms of communication to the patient is a first step towards possible improvements.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### First step: the hospital billing office
If you receive a hospital bill and do not understand how it was calculated, the first step is to contact the billing office of the facility where you were admitted. Ask them to explain the reason for the categorization and the base fee applied. They have the obligation to respond and provide you with access to the documents that led to the invoice (coding report, discharge report).
### Second step: request clinical documentation
If you are not satisfied with the hospital's explanations, you can formally request: - The coding report: the document that explains which diagnoses and procedures were recorded in your case - The discharge report: the complete clinical documentation of your stay
These documents contain details that do not appear on the invoice and allow you to check if the DRG classification is correct. They are yours by right and the hospital cannot deny access.
### Third step: escalation to the insurer
If you believe that the invoice is incorrect or that the tariff has been calculated incorrectly, you can ask your health insurer to carry out a review. The insurer has the tools and expertise to check whether the invoiced amount is consistent with the SwissDRG catalogue and the basic tariff of the hospital.
According to Prio Swiss, the insurance association, policyholders explicitly have the right to request a review. It is important to know that this right exists and that you can exercise it free of charge. Submit your request in writing, attaching documentation that supports your dispute.
### Fourth step: further escalation
If the insurer does not solve the problem to your satisfaction either, you can contact the Swiss Patients' Organisation, which offers advice and guidance on hospital billing issues and patient rights in Swiss healthcare.
### Practical checklist
✓ Request clarification from the hospital billing office ✓ Ask for a copy of the coding report and discharge report ✓ Compare the codes used with the SwissDRG catalogue (public) ✓ If you find any discrepancies, please contact your health insurer ✓ Ask for a formal review of the invoice in writing
Transparency in the Swiss healthcare system is not automatic: you have to activate it. Knowing these steps and your rights is the first step to really understanding what you are paying when you receive a hospital bill.
You can find out more about how premiums and health cover work in Switzerland in our guide to health insurance.

item.title: KVG premiums Fribourg: deductibles and subsidies 2026
item.description: KVG deductibles in the Canton of Fribourg, how to choose, procedures for accessing the premium reduction and official deadlines 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - KVG is mandatory for all residents of Fribourg; signing within 3 months of arrival - Deductibles: 6 choices of CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500 — lowest premium with high deductible - Premium reduction: cantonal subsidy for low incomes; annual application by the end of February - Premiums change every year; cancellation by 30 November to change insurer from 1 January
## Key Facts - What: Compulsory health insurance (KVG) managed on a private basis by authorised insurers - Where: Canton of Fribourg and all of Switzerland - When: Subscription within 3 months of arrival; Rewards renewed every January 1st - Who: Each resident must enter into a contract with a private insurer - Deductibles: 6 options (CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500) - Cantonal subsidy: For incomes below the cantonal threshold - Deadlines: Change of insurer by 30 November; subsidy request by the end of February
KVG (compulsory health insurance) is the health protection system that protects every resident of Switzerland, including the canton of Fribourg. Unlike pension or unemployment insurance, KVG is entirely privatised: it is not a federal tax, but a policy taken out directly with an authorised commercial insurer. Every resident has a legal obligation to take out within three months of arriving in the canton; those who fail to do so lose their right to cantonal subsidies and risk administrative fines.
### Why each canton manages subsidies differently The federal system sets the basic rules for KVG (standardised deductibles, minimum coverage, equity monitoring), but the canton of Fribourg manages premium reduction subsidies itself. This means that the income criteria, the amount of the benefit, the application deadlines and the required documents vary from canton to canton. An income that entitles you to the subsidy in Fribourg may not entitle you in another region. For this reason, direct consultation with the Fribourg administration is essential to learn about the specific rules for 2026.
### The deductibles available in Freiburg All licensed insurers in Switzerland, including those operating in Fribourg, offer six deductible options for adults: CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500. The deductible is the amount that each insured pays in full out of pocket before the insurance company starts covering medical costs. A deductible of CHF 300 implies a higher annual premium, as the insurer covers almost all costs over CHF 300. Conversely, a deductible of CHF 2500 requires a much lower premium, because the insured assumes a higher risk. The choice depends on medical consumption habits, economic situation and family needs.
### The prizes change every year and the exchange procedure Every autumn, the individual insurers communicate the new premiums for the following year. In the canton of Fribourg, as in the whole of Switzerland, anyone wishing to change insurers or increase their chosen deductible (to save on premiums) is entitled to cancel their policy by 30 November of the current year. Termination must be made in accordance with the contractual procedures (usually by registered letter or cantonal form). The effect of the termination is 1 January of the following year: the contract ends and the new one begins. This mechanism allows everyone to adapt their coverage to the new premium levels without penalty. ### How the premium reduction subsidy works at cantonal level The canton of Fribourg finances a subsidy for residents who are unable to pay the KVG premium for economic reasons. This subsidy (also referred to as "premium reduction" or "contributions" depending on the canton) is an annual payment based on income and assets. Unlike other federal social benefits (such as AHV/AHV or unemployment), entitlement to KVG benefits is managed exclusively by the canton; there are no uniform federal rules. Each Swiss canton therefore sets its own criteria, amounts and procedures independently.
### Who is entitled to the Fribourg cantonal subsidy The entitlement is triggered when the annual KVG premium exceeds a certain percentage of the declared gross income. In most cantons, this threshold varies from 5% to 8%, but the canton of Fribourg sets the precise value each year and publishes it on its official website. In addition, the canton considers movable and immovable assets. Couples, families with minor children and single people have different income thresholds; the canton applies growth factors for each family member. The data declared in the cantonal tax return of the previous year are used to assess eligibility.
### Practical scenario: who benefits Imagine a single person residing in Fribourg with a gross annual income of CHF 32,000 (about CHF 2,666/month). If you choose a deductible of CHF 500, the annual premium could be CHF 2,800. The premium-to-income ratio is 2,800 ÷ 32,000 = 8.75%. If the Fribourg cantonal threshold is set at 7%, this person exceeds the threshold and is eligible for the subsidy. The canton could cover CHF 400-600 per year, reducing the actual cost of the premium and making coverage more affordable.
### What happens if the subsidy is refused If the canton denies the subsidy, the reason must be communicated by official letter. The refusal can occur if the income is above the threshold, the assets are excessive, or the documentation is incomplete. In these cases, the applicant has the right to lodge an appeal with the cantonal appeal authority within the deadline set by the canton (check the official deadline with the office). The appeal must justify the office's error: misdeclared data, miscalculated threshold, documents not considered correctly. If the application is incomplete, the canton usually notifies and asks for the missing documents before refusing.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### How to apply for the KVG subsidy in Fribourg
Step 1: Check your pre-eligibility Calculate the ratio between the annual KVG premium (visible in the bulletin received from the insurer) and your gross income declared on the last cantonal tax return form. If the report exceeds the threshold published by the Canton of Fribourg (check the official website of the social benefits section), you are potentially eligible.
Step 2: Gather the required documentation Prepare: copy of the KVG policy confirmation letter (insurance certificate), last premium slip received from the insurer, tax return from the previous year (Fribourg cantonal form), copy of identity card or passport, and ownership documents or rental agreement (if applicable).
Step 3: Fill out the cantonal form Download the application form from the official website of the Canton of Fribourg (section dedicated to social benefits or social assistance). Fill it out legibly, including: name and address, KVG insurance number, gross income of the previous year, declared assets.
Step 4: Submit the application to the relevant office Send the completed form plus attachments to the Fribourg cantonal office responsible for social benefits. The methods vary: delivery in person at the office (during opening hours), sending by traditional mail (registered mail recommended), or sending by certified email (if the cantonal website allows it).
Step 5: Wait for the official response The canton examines the application and communicates the decision by official letter within the stipulated time frame (usually 2-4 weeks). If eligible, you will receive a communication with the annual amount of the subsidy. If rejected, the letter must state the reason.
Step 6: If refused, appeal You have the right to lodge a written appeal with the Fribourg cantonal appeals authority within the official cantonal deadline (check with the office upon receipt of the rejection letter). The appeal must justify the error, attaching new evidence or clarifications if available.
### Important deadlines and contacts
The application for the benefit must usually be submitted by the end of February of the year for which you apply for it (to receive the benefit from January). Changes in deductible or insurer can occur by cancelling the policy by November 30 of each year, with effect from January 1 of the following year. You can submit a new application for the benefit each year if your economic situation changes.
For exact contacts, up-to-date information on the 2026 income criteria and specific Fribourg deadlines, consult the official website of the Canton of Fribourg (social benefits section). You can also use the [calcolatore LAMal](nav:health) to estimate how much money you can save by choosing different deductibles or accessing the cantonal subsidy.
